what_its_for: Alectinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of lung cancer called ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It works by blocking a protein (ALK) that tells cancer cells to grow and spread. Your doctor has confirmed your cancer has this specific protein change, which means alectinib is designed to target your type of cancer.
how_to_take: Take alectinib capsules by mouth with food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not open, crush, or chew them. Taking it with a meal helps your body absorb the medicine better and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take your doses at the same times each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: The usual dose is 4 capsules (600 mg total) taken twice a day with food, for a total of 8 capsules per day. Each capsule is 150 mg. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on how you are tolerating the medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 6 hours away. If your next dose is within 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store alectinib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and store it in the original container. Protect it from moisture and heat. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid sunlight and tanning beds as much as possible, because alectinib can make your skin more sensitive to the sun. Use sunscreen (SPF 50 or higher), wear protective clothing, and wear a hat when outdoors. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can affect how your body processes the medicine. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, especially St. John's Wort, as it can reduce how well alectinib works. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: shortness of breath, chest pain, or a new or worsening cough (could be a lung problem); fast or irregular heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting; severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine (could be muscle breakdown); yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (could be liver problems); unusual swelling in your hands, feet, or legs; vision changes; signs of infection such as fever or chills. These side effects can be serious and need prompt medical attention.
when_it_works: Alectinib does not cure cancer, but it works to slow or stop the cancer from growing. Many patients begin to see results within the first few weeks to months of treatment, though it may take longer for your doctor to confirm the medicine is working through scans or tests. It is important to keep taking alectinib every day as prescribed, even if you feel well, because stopping the medicine can allow the cancer to grow again.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Alectinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for one week after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for one week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking alectinib and for one week after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have liver disease. Older adults: Older patients can take alectinib at the usual dose, but should watch closely for side effects and report any new symptoms to their doctor.
